neighbours.label: the first piece of a split sensory word for a smell, sound or feel (' must'|y, ' wh'|istling, ' clam'|my)
fire: The old cellar had a damp and musty odor all year.
A faint whistling came from the kettle in the kitchen.
Her forehead was pale and clammy when the nurse arrived.
Open the windows to clear that musty air from the attic.
The wind made a low whistling noise under the door.
His hands grew clammy as the elevator stopped.
Those old books smell musty after years in a box.
The boy's chest made a slight wheezing noise at night.
quiet: The old cellar had a damp and sour odor all year.
A faint humming came from the fridge in the kitchen.
Her forehead was pale and hot when the nurse arrived.
Open the windows to clear that stale air from the attic.
The wind made a low moaning noise under the door.
His hands grew numb as the elevator stopped.
Those old books smell sweet after years in a box.
The boy's chest made a slight rattling noise at night.

short: first piece of a sensory word
